answer.mechanism: Count exposed unit tile sides: P = 4N - 2E, where E is the number of shared sides.

results.evidence: The examples have (N,E) = (1,0), (2,1), (4,4), (4,3), and (4,0), giving 4, 6, 8, 10, and 16. In particular, the 2-by-2 block shares four sides, whereas the four-tile row shares three. The requested six-cell shape has five shared sides, so P = 24 - 10 = 14. These observations support this simple perimeter rule but cannot determine an unrestricted rule: another rule can agree on every observed configuration and differ on this six-cell shape.

answer.mechanism: Sum the number of segments toggled at each fixed digit position, using the symmetric difference of the old and new segment sets.

results.evidence: For 23 to 59, the left digit 2 to 5 turns b,e off and c,f on: four toggles. The right digit 3 to 9 turns f on: one toggle. Thus the prediction is 4+1=5. The examples give 11 to 77: 1+1=2; 12 to 21: 5+5=10; 88 to 88: 0; 00 to 88: 1+1=2. Finitely many examples do not establish a unique unrestricted rule; the value 5 is conditional on this mechanism.

results.evidence: Color each cell by the parity of row+column. Every permitted move changes color. A path visiting all 12 cells exactly once uses 11 moves, so its endpoints must have opposite colors. Both (1,1) and (3,3) have even row+column and hence the same color. Therefore no such path exists.

The third row violates its d equation, so the single visible error must be there. The unchanged second row gives 8+b congruent to 9 modulo 10, forcing hidden b=1. In row three, changing a cannot make 2a+3 even modulo 10; changing b to satisfy d=8 forces b=2, which would yield c=2 rather than 4; changing c leaves the faulty d equation untouched. Therefore only d can be wrong, and d=(16+3) mod 10=9. Checks for all repaired rows: row 1 has c=(2+14) mod 10=6 and d=(4+7) mod 10=1; row 2 has c=(4+2) mod 10=6 and d=(8+1) mod 10=9; row 3 has c=(8+6) mod 10=4 and d=(16+3) mod 10=9; row 4 has c=(6+18) mod 10=4 and d=(12+9) mod 10=1. Exhaustive enumeration of all hidden digits and single visible-digit replacements found exactly this repair.

Exhaustive enumeration of all 2^12=4096 bit strings, testing each of their nine windows for either 0000 or 1111, counts 2242 strings with at least one highlight. Equivalently, the number a_n avoiding any run of four identical bits satisfies a_1=2, a_2=4, a_3=8 and a_n=a_(n-1)+a_(n-2)+a_(n-3) for n>=4, giving a_12=1854. Thus the probability is (4096-1854)/4096=1121/2048. The value 1/16 applies to 1111 in one prespecified window. It omits both the scan across positions and the willingness to highlight 0000. This calculation does not assume overlapping windows are independent.
